answers.reason: The senate decides on university-wide strategy and the student representative only acts for their faculty.
The budget planning round allocates funds university-wide and is not a faculty-specific student matter.
Appointment committees select professors, which is not part of the student representative's specific matters.
The elected student representative speaks for students in the faculty council of their faculty.
Study commissions deal with degree programmes and teaching, which concerns the students represented by the student representative.
Examination boards decide on individual student examination matters rather than general student representation.
The internal research funding round handles research grants for researchers, not student representation.
Module revisions are specific degree programme tasks handled by working groups, not the student representative body.
Laboratory equipment procurement is for teaching labs, not student representation.
Orientation week planning is for new students and typically involves student representatives, but the text restricts members to their single place of decision.
